Novak Djokovic delivered a clinical 6-3, 6-4, 6-2 demolition of Stefanos Tsitsipas ('no chinks in the Djokovic armour' per Reuters) to reach Round 3 against Arthur Rinderknech [25]; already trading at 16% on Kalshi and 13/2 at UK books before the match, clearing his toughest early test in straight sets lifts Djokovic +0.030 from 0.110 to 0.140. Ahead of Thursday's bottom-half R2, Taylor Fritz (17/2 at UK books, 7% Kalshi, 5-0 recent H2H over Zverev) moves clearly into #3 at 0.070 (+0.010) ahead of Alexander Zverev (drifted to 9/1 after disclosing a grass allergy and acknowledging his struggles on the surface, trimming 0.060 -> 0.055). Alex de Minaur trims slightly (0.035 -> 0.030; Kalshi only 2% given his lopsided H2H vs Sinner, though his soft Q3 path still edges Daniil Medvedev ~0.022 who faces Sinner in Q1). Top-5 sum rises to 0.870 with 0.130 on the narrowed field (Medvedev, Berrettini, FAA, Hurkacz, Paul, Fonseca, Mensik, Fils, Tiafoe).

questions.current_reasoning: Major Wimbledon Day 3 (July 1) upset reshapes the women's draw: 2024 champion Barbora Krejcikova rallied to eliminate No. 5 seed and reigning French Open champion Mirra Andreeva 4-6, 7-5, 6-4 in R2 (previously 0.095 -> 0.00). Andreeva was top seed Aryna Sabalenka's biggest Quarter 1 obstacle; Sabalenka had already risen to 26% (+285) on Kalshi on July 1 morning following shaky R1 three-setters from Rybakina and Swiatek, and after fighting off four set points to beat McCartney Kessler 6-1, 7-6(9) while seeing Andreeva exit Q1, Sabalenka surges from 0.20 to 0.265 (tempered slightly by facing big-hitting Jelena Ostapenko in R3). No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina (14% on Kalshi pre-Day 3, faces Caty McNally in R2 Thursday) edges up to 0.120. Two stronger contenders replace Andreeva and Coco Gauff in our top five: No. 4 seed Jessica Pegula (9% on Kalshi pre-Day 3) dispatched Sara Sorribes Tormo 7-6(6), 6-1 to reach a soft R3 vs Jessica Bouzas Maneiro and enters at 0.085; 2025 finalist Amanda Anisimova (No. 4 on Kalshi at 10% pre-Day 3 after a dominant 6-3, 6-2 R1 win, plays Sofia Kenin Thursday) enters at 0.085. Defending champion Iga Swiatek (9% on Kalshi after a tearful, 9-double-fault R1 struggle vs Townsend, faces Karolina Pliskova Thursday with Svitolina out of Q3) trims to 0.075. Coco Gauff drops just outside the top five (~0.065; 7% on Kalshi pre-Day 3, needed a 6-point tiebreak rally from 4-7 down to escape Solana Sierra 6-3, 3-6, 7-6(10-7)), leaving 37.0% on the deep field (Gauff, Keys, Muchova, Osaka, Krejcikova, Bencic, Jovic, Ostapenko, Paolini).

questions.title: Which team will win the England–India T20 international series in July 2026?
questions.background: India and England are scheduled to contest a T20 international series in England.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official match results or contemporaneous AFP reporting identifying the winner of the England–India T20 international series in July 2026. Resolution Timing : Resolve when a team secures an unassailable series lead, or when the series concludes if its winner has not previously been determined. Accepted Answer Format : The country name of the series-winning team.
questions.current_reasoning: Two concrete June 30 squad updates on the eve of the July 1 series opener at Durham nudge this five-match series 3% back toward India (England 0.58 -> 0.55, India 0.42 -> 0.45): (1) ECB named England's playing XI for the 1st T20I (Salt, Buttler, Brook, Bethell, Banton, Curran, Jacks, Dawson, Rashid, Luke Wood, Saqib Mahmood—9 of their March 2026 T20 World Cup semifinal XI) with frontline fast bowlers Jofra Archer and Josh Tongue rested following the New Zealand Test series before rejoining for Match 2 at Old Trafford on July 4; (2) Sky Sports and IANS report mystery spinner Varun Chakravarthy—previously thought absent on June 28 and historically lethal against England's aggressive batting—has returned to India's 16-man squad for the England leg (though PTI's 15-man list omitted him). Durham's seam-friendly surface (138 avg T20I score), India's continuing absence of Bumrah, Hardik Pandya, and Suryakumar Yadav, and lingering batting vulnerability after their shock 0-2 sweep in Ireland still keep home England slight favorites (~51% Match 1 without Archer/Tongue, ~53.5% Matches 2-5 -> ~55.6% across five matches).

questions.title: Which Chinese province will evacuate the most people in preparation for Typhoon Bavi by July 11, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Chinese authorities' figures in contemporaneous news coverage. Resolve to the Chinese province with the largest reported number of people evacuated in preparation for Typhoon Bavi as of July 11, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-07-11 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the province's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major July 1 meteorological update: HKO/Dimsum Daily (July 1, 9:34 PM HKT), China Daily/NMC (July 1, 10:18 PM CST), Stars & Stripes, Fox Weather (July 1, 6:16 PM EDT), and Luso Meteo confirm a live naming race between TWO active tropical systems for the next JMA name 'Bavi' (loser gets 'Maysak'): (1) Tropical Storm 09W (formerly Invest 95W) east of Guam—already upgraded to TS by JTWC (40 mph) and forecast to rapidly intensify into a Cat 4/5 super typhoon through the Marianas (July 6) before tracking WNW toward Taiwan or the Taiwan-Okinawa gap around July 10-11, where East China pre-emptive evacuations overwhelmingly concentrate in Zhejiang (~48%) and Fujian (~40%), with small Guangdong/Jiangsu/Shanghai tails; and (2) a South China Sea tropical depression (54 km/h, 880 km SE of Qionghai) forecast by China's NMC to reach TS/typhoon strength within 24 hours, make first landfall between eastern Hainan and western Guangdong on Friday July 3, and second landfall in Guangxi on Saturday July 4 (heavy >400mm rain), where evacuations split largely between Hainan (~48%), Guangdong (~44%), and Guangxi (~8%). Weighting the naming race ~62% to rapidly consolidating JTWC TS 09W and ~38% to the SCS depression yields Zhejiang 0.30 (#1, +0.03), Fujian 0.25 (-0.01), Guangdong 0.20 (sharp drop from 0.33), Hainan 0.18 (major jump from 0.07), and Guangxi 0.03 (replacing Jiangsu), leaving 4% for Jiangsu/Shanghai/no major China evacuation.

questions.title: If Bavi makes landfall in mainland China during July 2026, which province will it strike first?
questions.background: Landfall occurs when a tropical cyclone's center crosses the coastline. This question concerns only mainland China.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official landfall reports from China’s National Meteorological Center, supplemented by contemporaneous reporting from major news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the province containing the location of Bavi’s first mainland-China landfall during July 2026. Subsequent landfalls do not count. If no qualifying landfall occurs during that month, the question is void. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Major July 1 meteorological update: Two active systems are racing on July 1-2 for the JMA name 'Bavi': (1) JTWC Tropical Storm 09W east of Guam (~62% prior to take 'Bavi'), projected by ECMWF/GFS ensembles to approach Taiwan or pass between Taiwan and Okinawa around July 10-11 (with ~75% chance of mainland China landfall, concentrated in Fujian ~44% and Zhejiang ~42%, plus ~8% Guangdong and ~6% northern coastal tail); and (2) a South China Sea tropical depression (~38% prior to take 'Bavi') forecast by China's NMC to intensify within 24h and make near-certain (~95%) China landfall on Friday July 3 along the coast between eastern Hainan and western Guangdong before hitting Guangxi on July 4. Conditioning strictly on a qualifying mainland China landfall via Bayes' rule shifts posterior weights to ~58% 09W and ~42% SCS system (incorporating a small nuance if Hainan Island vs continental mainland triggers Guangxi/Guangdong), shifting probabilities sharply from June 24 climatology: Fujian 0.26, Zhejiang 0.24 (+0.04), Hainan 0.22 (+0.10), Guangdong 0.20 (-0.12), and Guangxi 0.04, with 4% tail on Shanghai/Jiangsu/Shandong. JMA's naming call on July 2 will cleanly bifurcate this distribution.
